name: Nodular Lichen Myxedematosus

criteria.description: Presence of multiple waxy, firm, flesh-colored to erythematous nodules predominantly on the limbs and trunk
Skin biopsy showing dermal mucin deposition with fibroblast proliferation without evidence of systemic involvement
No clinical or laboratory evidence of systemic mucinosis or paraproteinemia
Absence of monoclonal gammopathy on serum protein electrophoresis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: characteristic clinical presentation, confirmatory histopathology, and absence of systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of scleromyxedema and systemic mucinoses

pathognomonic.symptomName: Waxy, firm, flesh-colored to erythematous dermal nodules
searchTerms: hard dermal nodules with waxy feel

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized dermal mucin deposition confirmed by biopsy
searchTerms: dermal mucin deposits confirmed by biopsy

common.symptomName: Symmetrical distribution of nodules on extremities and trunk
searchTerms: symmetrical nodules on limbs and trunk
nodules on both sides of body

common.symptomName: Slow progression of nodular lesions over months

occasional.symptomName: Localized skin induration adjacent to nodules
Mild joint stiffness near affected skin areas
searchTerms: slight joint tightness by skin lesions

occasional.symptomName: Occasional mild pain or tenderness at nodular sites

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as fatigue or malaise

searchTerms: weakness or pain in hands and feet
nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs

laboratory: Normal serum protein electrophoresis without monoclonal gammopathy
imaging: Not typically required; imaging may be used to exclude systemic involvement
other: Skin biopsy showing increased dermal mucin and fibroblast proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic involvement including neurological and cardiac symptoms
Limited to papular lesions without nodules
Less prominent fibroblast proliferation on biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with systemic symptoms
Neurological deficits or signs of systemic involvement
references: Wollina U. Nodular lichen myxedematosus: clinical and histopathological features. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2017;31(4):e183-e185.
Rongioletti F, Rebora A. Updated classification of papular mucinosis, lichen myxedematosus, and scleromyxedema. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2001;44(2):273-281.
